newsitem.title: UK: Clean tanker rates weak in Mideast, Asia.
newsitem.headline: Clean tanker rates weak in Mideast, Asia.

text.p: Clean tanker rates were mostly weaker, particularly in the Middle East with demand elsewhere confirming a slack market on most routes, brokers said.
Shipping brokers E.A. Gibson said in a weekly report the market was dogged by the lack of firm enquiry with the calm persisting in most loading areas both East and West.
They reported a very quiet week in the Middle East, with few charterers fixing larger size cargoes and a number of deals failing.

A 70,000 tonne cargo to South Korea was fixed on Friday at W160 while 49,500 tonne business into India fell to W165. This compares with W180-185 for 42,000 tonne vessels to India and W230-W235 for 30,000 tonners last week.
"Vessels have started to build up in the Middle East and rate levels are destined for further decline," the report said.
"It is definitely down in the Med but stable on Cross U.K./Cont," a broker said.

Gibson said cross-Med rates picked up later in the week with naphtha cargoes done at W200 for 27,250 tonnes in cross-Med trade but still below last week's levels of W205-W215 for small 30,000 tonners.
Gas oil fixtures were done at W175 for 25,000 tonne business ex-Ventspils.
The Caribbean market remained depressed with rates sliding to W185/190 from W205 for 30,000 tonne vessels last week.
Gibson said rates could rise with a few expected Venezuelan tenders to be awarded later this month.
"In the U.K./Cont...any change to the longer-haul trading has been short-lived and even moving clean products from Northwest Europe to the States has been less than of recent," the report said.
There was only one fixture reported in the week at W155 basis 33,000 tonnes.
